q: Do RE100 and CDP accept unbundled RECs from India?
title: Do RE100 and CDP accept Indian RECs?
short: Yes, if each certificate passes their tests. Neither rejects Indian RECs or I-RECs as a class. RE100 checks tracking, retirement in your name, vintage, market boundary and, from 2024, that the plant is no more than 15 years old. CDP takes market-based Scope 2 figures that meet the GHG Protocol Scope 2 Quality Criteria.

sections.h: The checks a certificate must pass
ol: Issued in a recognised tracking system: the India REC registry or the I-REC registry.
Retired or redeemed in your company's name, with a record you can show.
Vintage close to the period of the electricity you claim, normally the same reporting year.
Same market as your consumption. India's national grid is one market for this purpose.
For RE100, the generating plant was commissioned or repowered within the last 15 years, with limited exemptions such as some long-term contracts.
Not counted twice: not used for a renewable purchase obligation, and not sold again.

ul: Old plants: certificates from wind or hydro commissioned more than 15 years ago fail the RE100 age test.
Vintage mismatch: buying old certificates to cover the current year.
No retirement proof in the company's own name, only a broker's statement.
The same units counted toward a discom's or company's renewable obligation.

sections.h: How it shows up in your reporting
p: Certificates affect only your market-based Scope 2. Your location-based Scope 2, using the CEA grid factor, stays the same. Report both, and in CDP give the certificate type, country, vintage, volume and commissioning year of the plant.

sections.h: Bundled options that avoid most of these questions
p: An on-site solar plant, a power purchase agreement or a green tariff from your discom carries the renewable attribute with the power. These are generally treated as stronger evidence than unbundled certificates, but you still need the contract or tariff document.

senseible: Senseible reports location-based Scope 2 from your bills and market-based Scope 2 when you add certificate or contract data. It does not buy, sell or retire RECs, and it does not check certificates against RE100 or CDP criteria.
